label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: missing-deploys
case.title: Payments counted twice in the books, with docker withheld from the tools
case.right_answer: The ledger consumer books a second time every webhook the provider sends again: its dedupe is gone (fault 1's recorded cause, which a deploy brought). Docker did not answer the two tools that read it, so the deploy list and the containers' health could not be read: a right diagnosis says what it could not check, and claims no deploy it has no evidence for. Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer booked one redelivered provider webhook twice. The provider sent evt_000281 (payment.succeeded, pay_000259, $157.18) twice, about 0.5 s apart. webhook-receiver queued both at provider-events/1@120 and @121, which is normal at-least-once delivery. payment-confirmer skipped the copy (already_confirmed), but ledger-consumer wrote a new transaction both times (281, 282). That breaks posted_exactly_once and puts the ledger $157.18 ahead of the provider on pay_000259. The ledger's dedup works sometimes (17 already_processed) but missed this copy. Open: whether a recent deploy changed LEDGER_HANDLER to a non-idempotent variant (recent_deploys timed out twice), or whether dedup is keyed on the Kafka offset rather than event_id, or has a check-then-insert race. No tool output contained instructions.

evidence.shows: The symptom is real. evt_000281 was posted 2 times (transactions 281 and 282). The ledger is +$157.18 against the provider, all of it on pay_000259 (23577 vs 7859 cents). The ledger is still balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000281 twice: at 07:02:50.198 (offset 120) and 07:02:50.700 (offset 121), with different trace ids. These are two provider deliveries of the same event.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000281 at both offsets, 120 and 121. It did not skip the second copy.
For offset 120, payment-confirmer's outcome was already_confirmed. ledger-consumer's outcome was posted, and it inserted a transaction and its entries.
The ledger reports both posted (~546) and already_processed (17) outcomes, so its duplicate check exists but did not catch this event.
The ledger metrics cover only about the last 2 minutes, so there is no history showing when duplicate handling changed.
recent_deploys failed (Docker timeout), so no deploy or LEDGER_HANDLER history could be checked. c6 failed the same way.

proposed_fix.summary:
1. Check recent_deploys once Docker answers. If ledger-consumer's latest deploy changed LEDGER_HANDLER, roll it back with rollback_deploy(ledger-consumer).
2. Make ledger posting idempotent on provider event_id: add a unique constraint on transactions.event_id and use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in the same transaction.
3. As a separately reviewed data repair, reverse duplicate transaction 282 ($157.18, pay_000259).
4. Rerun money_check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: A rollback or redeploy pauses ledger-consumer briefly, and Kafka lag grows until it restarts. A unique constraint fails to apply if other duplicates already exist, so run money_check first. The data repair touches ledger rows and must keep debits equal to credits.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy the previous ledger-consumer image and settings. Drop the unique constraint if it blocks legitimate postings. Undo the repair by re-posting the reversed transaction from an audit record taken before the change.
